Services.title: One team for everything you ship.
Services.text: Berox is an Egypt-based software agency. We design, build and support websites, web apps, Flutter mobile apps for iOS and Android, custom software and SaaS products, AI chatbots and workflow automation. One team handles design, development and post-launch support for businesses in Egypt, the Gulf and worldwide.

Process.title: A clear path from idea to launch.
Process.text: A Berox project has five steps: discover, design, build, launch, and support and grow. After a free intro call we agree scope, timeline and price. You approve the design before any code is written, we show working demos while building, then we test, deploy and hand everything over.

items.title: Design

items.title: Build
items.text: We develop in short cycles and show you working progress along the way.

items.title: Launch

items.title: Support & Grow

WhyBerox.title: Everything you need to launch, under one roof.
WhyBerox.text: Berox combines strategy, design and engineering in one team, so web, mobile and backend are built together. You own the code, designs and infrastructure, you approve the design before development, and you see working demos along the way. After launch we provide monitoring, fixes and ongoing improvements.

Faq.title: Questions, answered before you ask.
Faq.text: Pricing, timelines and what we need from you, explained plainly. Can’t find your question? Talk to us.

items.q: How do you price your projects?
items.a: Most projects are fixed-scope and fixed-price. After a discovery call you receive a written proposal with the scope, milestones and one total price, so there are no surprises.

items.q: Can you work on an hourly or monthly basis instead?
items.a: Yes. For ongoing or evolving work we offer a monthly retainer or a dedicated team, billed on a predictable schedule.

items.q: What affects the cost of a project?
items.a: Mainly the number of screens and features, the complexity of integrations, custom design, and how much content needs to be created. A clearer brief means a more accurate quote.

items.q: How does payment work?
items.a: Payment is split by milestone, with a deposit to reserve your start date. Each stage is invoiced only when it is delivered and approved.

items.q: Are there any hidden costs?
items.a: No. The proposal lists everything that is included. Third-party costs such as hosting, domains, app store accounts and paid APIs are listed separately, and those accounts stay in your name.

items.q: What happens if the scope changes mid-project?
items.a: Changes are welcome. We write up the impact on cost and timeline first, and work on the change starts only after you approve it in writing.

items.q: How much does a mobile app cost in Egypt?
items.a: The cost depends on the number of screens and features, integrations, custom design and the content to be created. We do not publish a fixed price list because every app is different. After a discovery call you receive a written proposal with one total price, split by milestone.

items.q: How much does a website cost in Egypt?
items.a: The price depends on the number of pages, the features, custom design and how much content must be written. A business website usually takes 2–4 weeks. After a discovery call you receive a written proposal with the scope, milestones and one total price.

items.q: Do you build online stores (e-commerce)?
items.a: Yes. Our in-house Bazaro project is a reference store with a guest cart, cart drawer, filters, search and checkout with two payment options. Tell us what you want to sell and we will plan the build together.

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: A business website usually takes 2–4 weeks. Web apps and mobile apps typically take 4–8 weeks, depending on features and integrations. Your proposal includes dated milestones.

items.q: Can you deliver an MVP quickly?
items.a: Yes. We can start with the smallest version that proves your idea, launch it, and build on real user feedback instead of guessing.

items.q: What can delay a project?
items.a: Most delays come from late content, scattered feedback or scope changes. Agreeing on review windows and a single approver at the start keeps things on track.

items.q: How often will I see progress?
items.a: You get regular updates and a working demo at the end of each milestone, so you review real progress rather than status reports.

items.q: Do you offer rush delivery?
items.a: Sometimes. If your deadline is fixed, we can reduce the scope or add resources to meet it, and we will tell you honestly what is realistic.

items.q: When can you start?
items.a: Start dates depend on our current schedule. Once you approve the proposal and pay the deposit, we confirm a start date in writing.

items.q: How long does it take to build a SaaS product or MVP?
items.a: A first version of a web app or SaaS product typically takes 4–8 weeks, depending on features and integrations. We start with the smallest version that proves your idea, launch it, and extend it based on real user feedback.

items.q: What do you need from me to get started?
items.a: A clear goal, your brand assets (logo, colors, fonts), any existing content, and one point of contact who can approve work. If something is missing, we can help you create it.

items.q: I only have an idea. Can you still help?
items.a: Absolutely. We start with a discovery session to define the problem, the users and the scope, then turn it into a clear plan and estimate.

items.q: How do I start a project with you?
items.a: Contact us with a short description of your goals. We schedule a call, send a proposal, and begin once you approve it.

items.q: Do I need technical knowledge?
items.a: No. We explain decisions in plain language and handle the technical side, while you focus on your business and on approvals.

items.q: Do you sign an NDA?
items.a: Yes. We are happy to sign a non-disclosure agreement before you share any confidential details about your product or business.

items.q: Who writes the content and provides the images?
items.a: You can provide them, or we can help with copywriting, design and image sourcing. Content is the most common cause of delays, so we plan it early.

items.q: What is the difference between a website and a web app?
items.a: A website mainly presents information, such as a company, its services or a store catalog. A web app lets users complete tasks, such as logging in, managing data or placing orders. Many projects combine both, and we help you choose the simplest option that meets your goal.

items.q: What is your development process?
items.a: We move through discovery, design, development, testing and launch. Each phase ends with a review so you can approve before we continue.

items.q: How will we communicate?
items.a: You get one point of contact, a shared channel for day-to-day questions, and scheduled check-ins. We aim to reply to messages within one business day.

items.q: Will I review the design before development starts?
items.a: Yes. You approve the design, usually as an interactive prototype, before any development begins, which avoids costly rework later.

items.q: Which technologies do you use?
items.a: We choose tools to fit your goals: modern web frameworks for websites and web apps, and Flutter for iOS and Android apps from a single codebase.

items.q: How do you make sure the quality is high?
items.a: We test on real devices and browsers, check performance and accessibility, and fix issues before launch. You also get a review period to check everything yourself.

items.q: Do you work with clients outside Egypt?
items.a: Yes. We work remotely with clients worldwide, in English and Arabic, across time zones.

items.q: What is Flutter and why do you use it for mobile apps?
items.a: Flutter is Google's open-source framework for building iOS and Android apps from a single codebase. One codebase means one team builds both apps together, which can reduce build time and maintenance compared with building two separate native apps.

items.q: Do you work with clients in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and the Gulf?
items.a: Yes. We work remotely, in English and Arabic, and plan calls around your time zone, whether you are in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman or elsewhere. Every project follows the same written proposal, milestones and ownership terms.

items.q: Who owns the code and design?
items.a: You do. Once the final payment is made, all source code, designs and accounts are transferred to you.

items.q: Do I get access to the code during development?
items.a: Yes. We can work in a repository that you own, so you can follow progress and are never locked in.

items.q: Are my data and my customers’ data secure?
items.a: We follow security best practices: encrypted connections, controlled access and careful handling of credentials. Sensitive data is only used for your project.

items.q: Do you use third-party or open-source software?
items.a: Where it makes sense, yes. We use well-maintained libraries and tell you about any licenses that apply to your product.

items.q: Is there a written contract?
items.a: Yes. Every project has a written agreement that covers scope, timeline, payment terms, ownership and confidentiality.

items.q: Can I move my project to another team later?
items.a: Yes. We deliver clean, documented code and handover notes so another team can continue the work if you choose.

items.q: Do you support the project after launch?
items.a: Yes. Our Support & Growth plan covers updates, monitoring, fixes and new features after launch.

items.q: What if something breaks after launch?
items.a: Tell us and we will investigate right away. Support terms are agreed in your proposal, so you know what to expect.

items.q: Can you improve an existing website or app?
items.a: Yes. We review what you have, then fix, redesign or extend it, or migrate it to a modern stack.

items.q: Do you handle hosting and deployment?
items.a: Yes. We can set up and manage hosting, domains and automated deployment, or hand everything over to your own team.

items.q: Can you help my product grow after launch?
items.a: Yes. We help with performance, search visibility and new features, guided by how real users use your product.

items.q: How do I report an issue or request a change after launch?
items.a: Message us in the shared channel or by email. We confirm your request, estimate the effort if needed, and reply within one business day.

items.q: Can you build an AI chatbot for my business?
items.a: Yes. Chatbots and assistants are part of our AI & Automation service, and they can work in English, Arabic or both. Our AI Booking Assistant concept, for example, is designed to answer questions and book appointments in Egyptian Arabic.

projects.name: Bazaro
projects.summary: A full-featured e-commerce storefront built for everyday essentials.
projects.imageAlt: Bazaro home page on desktop and mobile
projects.overview: Bazaro is an e-commerce storefront we built to show what a complete shopping experience looks like from start to finish: browsing, cart, accounts and checkout. It is an in-house project by the Berox team, made as a working reference for what we deliver.
projects.challenge: Shoppers leave when buying feels slow or when they are asked to create an account too early. We wanted a store where anyone can start shopping immediately and an account is only requested when it matters.
projects.solution: A guest cart and wishlist that live in the browser and merge into the account after login, a cart that opens as a drawer without leaving the page, and a checkout with saved addresses and two payment options.
projects.featuresTitle: Everything a shopper needs, nothing in the way

features.title: A cart that starts with the visitor
features.text: Shoppers add products without an account, and the guest cart merges into their profile after login.

features.title: Cart drawer and cart page
features.text: A side panel on desktop and a bottom sheet on mobile, plus a full page for editing the order.

features.title: Filters, sorting and live search
features.text: Filter by category, brand and price, sort results and search products and brands from the navbar.

features.title: Product pages that sell
features.text: Image gallery, stock status, quantity selector, reviews breakdown and shipping details.

features.title: Complete accounts
features.text: Sign up, login and password recovery with a six-digit code, plus profile, address book and order history.

features.title: A clear checkout
features.text: Saved addresses with cash on delivery or card payment.

projects.name: AI Booking Assistant
projects.summary: An Egyptian-Arabic AI assistant that answers customer questions and books appointments for clinics, salons and similar businesses.
projects.imageAlt: Demo clinic website with the AI assistant chat widget on desktop and mobile
projects.overview: This is a concept and demo, not a client project. The AI Booking Assistant is an idea we designed at Berox for clinics, salons and similar businesses: a chat assistant that talks in Egyptian Arabic, answers customer questions and books appointments. The screens on this page are designed mockups with sample data, not a live product.
projects.challenge: Small businesses lose bookings when nobody picks up the phone or answers messages after hours. Customers also write in Egyptian Arabic and in Franco-Arabic, which many chatbots handle poorly.
projects.solution: An assistant designed to understand how customers actually write, answer questions about prices and hours, and book, change or cancel appointments inside the chat. When it is not sure, it hands the conversation to a staff member, and a simple dashboard lets the business review chats and edit prices and hours.

projects.name: Krakebak
projects.summary: A mobile app and a web dashboard that organize waste collection from homes, shops and centers: requests, couriers, regions, contracts and sales in one place.
projects.imageAlt: Krakebak admin dashboard on desktop with the mobile view on top
projects.overview: Krakebak is a client product for collecting waste materials from homes, shops and centers. Berox built it as a mobile app and a web admin dashboard in three weeks. The dashboard gives the operations team one place to manage supply requests, couriers, regions, contracts and sales.
projects.challenge: Collecting waste from homes, shops and centers means coordinating many requests, couriers and service areas at the same time. Each request has to reach the right courier, in the right region, and be followed until it is picked up and paid for.
projects.solution: A web dashboard in Arabic, with a right-to-left layout and dark and light themes. It tracks every supply request by status, ties couriers and requests to service regions on a map, manages courier contracts and wages, and records every change in an operations log. Suppliers, customers, sales representatives and sales orders live in the same place, and permissions are set by role so each person sees only what they need.

features.title: Supply request tracking
features.text: Every request is followed by status, such as pending assignment, scheduled today, failed pickup and payment due, with quick indicators on the home screen.

features.title: Couriers and join requests
features.text: Manage the courier team, review join requests and keep track of ratings.

features.title: Regions on a map
features.text: Service regions are drawn on a map and linked to couriers and requests, and requests outside coverage are flagged for review.

features.title: Waste catalog
features.text: A catalog of the waste types available in supply requests. Disabling a type hides it from new requests only.

features.title: Contracts, wages and expiry alerts
features.text: Courier contracts with their value and dates, wage statements, and alerts for contracts and papers that are about to expire.

features.title: Roles and an operations log
features.text: Permissions by role, and a read-only log of who did what and when.

projects.name: B-food
projects.summary: Scan, order, serve. One system from the customer's phone to the kitchen: customers scan a QR code and order, and the kitchen, bar and owner each get their own screen.
projects.imageAlt: B-food concept design: the restaurant dashboard on desktop and the QR menu on a phone
projects.overview: B-food is a design concept, not a delivered product. Customers scan a QR code at the table, browse an Arabic menu and send their order. The kitchen and bar see it instantly on their own screens, and the owner manages the menu, tables, stock, staff and reports from one dashboard. Development has not started, and every screen uses sample data.
projects.challenge: Many restaurants and cafes run orders, the kitchen, stock and staff on separate tools, or on paper. Orders get lost between the table and the kitchen, customers wait without knowing what is happening, and the owner sees the numbers late.
projects.solution: One system designed around the whole flow: a table-specific QR menu in Arabic for the customer, live screens for the kitchen and bar, and a single dashboard where the owner manages the menu, tables, recipe-based stock, staff and reports. It is designed to serve several branches from the same system.

projects.name: Stays
projects.summary: List your property, get booking requests, manage your calendar. Guests search by destination and dates, hosts manage listings and reservations, and the platform team reviews each listing.
projects.imageAlt: Stays concept design: the listings search on desktop and the search results on a phone
projects.overview: Stays is a design concept, not a delivered product, and the name is a working name. Guests search by destination, dates and number of guests and send a booking request. Hosts manage their listings, a calendar and reservations, and the platform team reviews each listing before it goes live. Development has not started, every screen uses sample data, and the listing photos are stock images.
projects.challenge: Small hosts often manage bookings through scattered messages and notes, and guests cannot see the full price before they ask. Platforms also need a way to check that listings are real before showing them.
projects.solution: A platform designed around three sides: guests who search and send a booking request with the price breakdown shown up front, hosts who accept or decline requests from their calendar, and a platform team that reviews listings before they are published. It is designed Arabic-first, right-to-left and mobile-first. Payments are not part of the concept shown here.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal information the Berox website collects, how we use it, and the choices you have. We keep it short and plain on purpose.
Privacy.contactText: Questions about this policy or your information? Reach us at:

blocks.text: Berox is a software agency based in Egypt. We design and build websites, web apps and mobile apps for clients around the world.
In this policy, “we”, “us” and “Berox” mean the team behind this website.
We only collect what you choose to send us through the contact form:

items: Your full name, company or brand name and phone number
Your email address, if you give it
Your project type, budget range and how you heard about us
Your project details, or your preferred contact method, day and time if you book a call

blocks.text: We do not ask for payment details, passwords or sensitive personal information. Please do not include them in your message.

This website does not keep a database of form submissions. When you submit the form, your device opens WhatsApp or your email app with your message already written. Nothing is sent until you press send there.
From that point, WhatsApp or your email provider handles the message under its own privacy policy.

items: To reply to your inquiry and arrange a call
To prepare a quote, scope and timeline for your project
To keep a record of our conversation while we work together

blocks.text: We do not sell or rent your information, and we do not send marketing messages unless you ask for them.
This website does not use advertising, tracking or analytics cookies.
It stores two small settings in your browser so the site works the way you expect:

items: Your language choice, kept in a cookie
Your light or dark theme, kept in your browser’s local storage

blocks.text: These settings are not used to identify you, and you can clear them at any time in your browser settings.

We share your information only with the services needed to run our business and answer you, such as WhatsApp, our email provider and our website hosting provider. We may also share it if the law requires us to.
Our hosting provider may keep standard server logs, such as IP address and browser type, to deliver and secure the website.

We keep your inquiry for as long as needed to respond and, if we work together, for the length of the project and any support. You can ask us to delete it at any time, unless the law requires us to keep it.

items: Tell you what information we hold about you
Stop using your information for a particular purpose

blocks.text: To make a request, contact us using the details below. We will reply within a reasonable time.

We take reasonable steps to protect your information, including using encrypted connections on this website. No method of sending data over the internet is completely secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.
This website is meant for businesses and adults. We do not knowingly collect information from children.
We may update this policy from time to time. The date at the top shows when it last changed. If we make a major change, we will say so on this page.
